evidence.claim: The government introduced measures to shield vulnerable groups from rising energy and food prices, including doubled energy assistance for 4 million households and lower electricity tariffs for low-consumption users.
evidence.title: Türkiye: OECD Economic Outlook, Volume 2022 Issue 2
evidence.excerpt: The government introduced measures to shield vulnerable groups from rising energy and food prices, including doubled energy assistance for 4 million households and lower electricity tariffs for low-consumption users.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: OECD country surveillance with specific distributional relief measures and household counts.
evidence.period_fit: Directly covers the 2022 policy response to the cost-of-living shock.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to the Erdogan government because it was a state response during his tenure, though it is mitigation rather than structural reform.
contrary_evidence: The same report warns that non-targeted price supports and energy dependence kept fiscal and inflation risks high.

evidence.claim: Employment recovered to pre-pandemic levels and income had been boosted by a 50% minimum-wage increase, but prices were rising further because of accommodative monetary policy, commodity prices, and exchange-rate depreciation, eroding real incomes.
evidence.title: Türkiye: OECD Economic Outlook, Volume 2022 Issue 1
evidence.excerpt: Employment recovered to pre-pandemic levels and income had been boosted by a 50% minimum-wage increase, but prices were rising further because of accommodative monetary policy, commodity prices, and exchange-rate depreciation, eroding real incomes.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: OECD surveillance text with specific labor, wage, inflation, and policy statements for the target year.
evidence.period_fit: Directly covers 2022 economic conditions and policy mix.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Erdogan-era macro policy because the accommodative monetary stance was the government-backed framework in place during 2022.
contrary_evidence: The minimum-wage increase provided some near-term household support.

evidence.claim: Real GDP grew 7.5% in the first half of 2022, tourism fully recovered, exporters benefited from supply-chain disruption, but investment remained subdued and macroeconomic imbalances rose.
evidence.title: Türkiye: OECD Economic Outlook, Volume 2022 Issue 2
evidence.excerpt: Real GDP grew 7.5% in the first half of 2022, tourism fully recovered, exporters benefited from supply-chain disruption, but investment remained subdued and macroeconomic imbalances rose.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: OECD country surveillance with specific 2022 growth, tourism, investment, and imbalance data.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable to Erdogan because the policy environment shaped investment and stabilization conditions, though some of the growth was externally driven.
contrary_evidence: The same passage says investment activity was subdued and imbalances rose.

evidence.claim: The IMF summarized the new policy model as relying on low interest rates, directing lending to selected sectors, and increasingly distortionary macrofinancial and regulatory measures; it also said inflation reached 85% in October 2022 and fiscal risks were rising.
evidence.title: Republic of Turkiye: 2022 Article IV Consultation-Press Release; and Staff Report
evidence.excerpt: The IMF summarized the new policy model as relying on low interest rates, directing lending to selected sectors, and increasingly distortionary macrofinancial and regulatory measures; it also said inflation reached 85% in October 2022 and fiscal risks were rising.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official IMF country report with a concise synthesis of the 2022 policy model, its consequences, and associated risks.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective but still about the 2022 consultation and 2022 outcomes.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strongly attributable to Erdogan because the low-rate model, directed credit, and intervention-heavy response were core government choices.
contrary_evidence: The same summary notes the public-debt burden remained low compared with peers.

evidence.claim: The man picked by President Tayyip Erdogan to oversee and articulate his unorthodox policy of driving down interest rates amid spiralling inflation and a tumbling currency was described as having little direct economic training.
evidence.title: Turkey’s new finance minister in the eye of a storm
evidence.excerpt: The man picked by President Tayyip Erdogan to oversee and articulate his unorthodox policy of driving down interest rates amid spiralling inflation and a tumbling currency was described as having little direct economic training.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire reporting is contemporaneous and specific, though the mirror is secondary hosting rather than the wire itself.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and relevant to the ruler-period economic team.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong attribution to Erdogan because the appointment was his and it signaled the type of economic team he preferred.
contrary_evidence: An AKP official in the same story argued Nebati worked closely with the president and had stemmed the collapse of the lira.

evidence.claim: Erdogan said gradually interest rates and inflation would fall and the lira would get firmer, with 2022 to be Turkey's brightest year.
evidence.title: Erdogan says working on steps to boost lira interest
evidence.excerpt: Erdogan said gradually interest rates and inflation would fall and the lira would get firmer, with 2022 to be Turkey's brightest year.
evidence.source_locator: Reuters wire summary in article body
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters wire quote from the ruler himself, although hosted on a secondary outlet.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct ruler attribution because the claim is Erdogan's own public economic guidance.
contrary_evidence: The broader article context describes the lira as volatile and the economy as under strain.

evidence.claim: The Turkish Ministry of Health, with WHO, UNICEF and NGOs, carried out a country-wide vaccination campaign to give missing doses to more than 400,000 refugee and migrant children under 5, reaching children in homes, communities and health centres.
evidence.title: WHO supports Turkey to ensure full immunization of refugee children
evidence.excerpt: The Turkish Ministry of Health, with WHO, UNICEF and NGOs, carried out a country-wide vaccination campaign to give missing doses to more than 400,000 refugee and migrant children under 5, reaching children in homes, communities and health centres.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: WHO directly describes a large, specific vaccination intervention and the ministry's role in implementation.
evidence.period_fit: The page was published in 2022 but describes a national campaign and the ongoing service-capacity model used during the ruler-period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong attribution to the Erdogan-era health authorities because the Ministry of Health implemented the campaign and WHO credits national technical cooperation.
contrary_evidence: The article also shows the program existed to remedy major access gaps created by displacement and mobility.

unresolved_gaps: Direct 2022 Turkish nuclear command-and-control or custody evidence is absent; the dossier mostly shows inherited treaty/NATO/IAEA posture plus civil-nuclear and mediation choices.
Direct forensic or documentary proof of Erdoğan's own assets, beneficial ownership, or personal enrichment in 2022 is still missing.
Independent corroboration beyond Reuters-style reporting is still thin for the media-control and family-access claims.
Audit-grade verification of project delivery and personnel effects is still thin; the package leans heavily on official program documents and self-reported completion counts.
